retrieved_synopses: COM moment with the Blood Merchant within Moonrise Towers

A merchant selling in the bazaar on the ground floor of Moonrise Tower. She is very interested in illithid-tainted blood from each race, which when traded grants a different kind of potion as a reward. The player can also learn her house's origins - and the fact that she's here to research the illithids.For nodes marked as OOM AND COM are in their own dialog fileFor nodes not marked as OOM or COM the dialog will have these speakers:1. Araj2. Group_Players (that might include Astarion since the default dialog and AOM version are pretty much the same).
The Blood Merchant hums to herself as she tinkers with her potions. After Astarion has bitten her, she gets into a really good mood.

The Mistress of Souls won't let us pass into Ketheric's chapel until we've completed MOO quests. Her tone is vaguely respectful, but not as deferential as a True Soul is used to. When we press her on this, we'll see her contempt - True Souls might be a big deal out in the world, but not here. In truth, she is a Myrkul cultist playing her role in the church of the Absolute, secretly contemptuous of every true believer.

You and Astarion are traveling as companions; in the night he reveals himself as a vampire by hunching over your bedroll to feed and is caught when you wake and fight him off. He reacts with alarm and pleading, insisting he rarely kills for food (feeding on animals) and begging for a small taste to restore his strength so he can continue helping you against the shared threat (the worms/tadpole). If you press him he grows defensive and bargains; if you consent he eagerly drinks, becomes invigorated, and turns cocky and overconfident. Other campmates or larger plot threads (Shadowheart, camp activities, temple/curse matters) may be happening nearby but are not part of this immediate bedside confrontation.
context: You’re in the Moonrise Towers bazaar with Araj Oblodra, the Blood Merchant who researches illithid-tainted blood and trades vials of different races for powerful potions. The scene is a companion (COM) moment: the player (addressed as “True Soul”) has already traded a vial, and Araj now asks for more—specifically a drop of the True Soul’s blood—and boldly offers a legendary-strength potion if Astarion bites her. Astarion is the player’s vampire companion (his vampirism was revealed earlier at camp) and is resistant to biting strangers; here he detects something “wrong” about Araj’s blood and balks. The player can press or persuade him while Araj grows flirtatious and impatient, framing the exchange as a tempting but risky bargain.
